reason: The cited lines show the tool discovers local Next.js servers, queries/list their MCP tools, and returns local server metadata including port, pid, command, localhost URL, and tool schemas/descriptions. That supports SECRET because local host/process/server information and localhost-derived content is returned to the agent. It also supports UNTRUSTED because tool metadata returned from locally running dev servers can be controlled by the server/project being queried. The lines do not themselves show arbitrary host code execution; any such behavior would have to be inside imported helpers such as getAllAvailableServers, so HOSTEXEC is insufficient. The lines also do not show agent-supplied data being exfiltrated or sent to an attacker-readable, agent-chosen destination; helper internals are not shown, so SINK is insufficient.
